item.title: MeshRepair: Autoregressive Topology Repair for Generated Artisan Meshes
item.description: arXiv:2610.14113v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent artisan mesh generation methods produce meshes whose topology comes close to the preferences of human artists. But gaps to artist quality remain because generated meshes commonly contain holes, stray faces, and duplicated faces. Regenerating a mesh from scratch is costly, and a new draw may change the preferred topology entirely or introduce errors elsewhere. In this work we study artisan topology correction. The task is to correct the topology of a generated mesh (the draft) in place, toward the layout an artist would make. We propose a method for this task. It is a face-level correction network based on a prefix-LM. It reads the mesh bidirectionally and emits an edit sequence autoregressively. The sequence consists of a deletion phase followed by an addition phase. We propose the novel formulation of the deletion head which picks faces to delete autoregressively and the addition head that selects vertices to form a face to add. The addition head also adds vertices when needed. Untouched faces pass through unchanged, so the corrected mesh keeps the vertices and the layout of the draft. The draft enters as a prefix and only the edits are generated. A correction therefore takes far fewer decoding steps than generating every face again with an autoregressive mesh generator. We benchmark our method against repair tools on scripted defects and on held-out drafts from two mesh generators. Across both scripted defects and generated drafts, our method improves the quad-equivalent face F1, removes non-manifold faces, and cleans up the topology.
item.dc:creator: Xiyu Wang, Yufei Wang, Ruocheng Wu, Zhihao Li, Lanqing Guo, Bihan Wen

item.title: Co-DSL: Human-LLM Co-design of Reusable Spatial Concepts for Layout Generation
item.description: arXiv:2610.15290v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present Co-DSL, a framework in which users and LLMs co-design reusable spatial concepts for layout generation. In the first stage, our system allows users to create a library of personalized operations. To add a concept, a user provides a description, which the LLM converts into an initial implementation. The user can then observe the concept's execution behavior over example scenarios and provide lightweight feedback to the LLM, which revises the concept's implementation logic. In the second stage, given a library, an LLM can author a layout program that meets a new layout request from a user. Executing a layout program instantiates a concept-graph, a declarative composition of library concepts. In this way, we require the LLM only to specify which concepts should hold, while we use a solver to search for a layout that satisfies them. Across five spatial layout domains, we find that Co-DSL libraries let LLMs capture layout patterns that are challenging for prior fixed-operation systems, and demonstrate that our concept-graph representation is needed for LLMs to reliably compose concepts together. We further find that Co-DSL lets LLMs author generative layout programs that expose high-level parametric controls users can manipulate to explore a distribution of related layouts without re-prompting.
item.dc:creator: R. Kenny Jones, Jiajun Wu, Maneesh Agrawala

item.title: Design for Machinability: Topology Optimization for Subtractive Machining Using Trimmed Neural Fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.15301v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topology optimization has found significant utility in additive manufacturing, but the resulting geometries are often difficult to realize using subtractive methods. The complex, curved surfaces of optimized designs typically require time-consuming point milling operations. In contrast, geometries composed of developable surfaces are well suited to flank milling, enabling substantial improvements in machining efficiency and surface quality. However, globally minimizing Gaussian curvature leads to overly simplistic designs. We address this challenge with a novel method that represents geometry using three implicit neural fields, optimized to produce machinable components. The resulting designs consist of regions of developable surfaces separated by seamlines where curvature is concentrated. Seamlines are efficiently computed as intersections of the implicit fields, while the geometry emerges through their product. By constraining surfaces to align with the cutter's normal or tangential direction, our approach further accommodates practical constraints of 3-axis machining. We demonstrate concurrent optimization of topology and Gaussian curvature, enabling control over seamline feature scale. Compared to methods that enforce subtractive machinability without considering milling efficiency, our approach consistently reduces machining time while maintaining competitive structural performance.
item.dc:creator: Hongrui Chen, Levent Burak Kara

item.title: Walk-on-Ambient-Patch: Solver-Adapted Isometric Embeddings for Projected Walk on Spheres
item.description: arXiv:2610.15573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Projected Walk on Spheres (PWoS) solves surface PDEs through ambient sampling and closest-point projection, but tightly folded embeddings can force short steps or ambiguous projections despite simple intrinsic geometry. We introduce Walk-on-Ambient-Patch (WoAP), which treats the embedding as a solver variable. Edge-isometry constraints and tangent-point repulsion separate intrinsically distant regions, optionally in higher codimension; patch states track residual projection branches without introducing PDE boundaries. We analyze the resulting geometry--sampling tradeoff: additional dimensions provide separation freedom but reduce uniform tangent progress, while strong tangent-biased proposals incur large importance-weight moments. Folded-surface experiments demonstrate reduced projection conflicts, a separate hard-constraint pilot verifies metric preservation, and an internal fixed-RMSE comparison favors higher dimensions at stricter accuracy targets. Together, these results motivate choosing the embedding and projection state jointly with the stochastic solver.
item.dc:creator: Yunfeng Liao, Xiucheng Li

item.title: Low-Cost Deep Learning for Automated Keyframe Interpolation in Sprite Animation
item.description: arXiv:2610.16423v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sprite-based animation remains prevalent in video game development, but manual in-betweening---generating intermediate frames between keyframes---is labor-intensive. Existing video frame interpolation methods, optimized for photorealistic content, introduce smoothing artifacts when applied to the sharp edges, limited color palettes, and stylized motion characteristic of hand-drawn sprites. We present a deep learning approach for sprite in-betweening that adapts a U-Net encoder-decoder architecture with domain-specific modifications, including RGBA-aware processing, multi-scale flow refinement, and alpha-gated blending to preserve pixel-perfect sprite aesthetics. Following data-centric AI principles, we demonstrate that a few carefully curated sprite animation triplets---selected for diversity, quality, and representative edge cases---enable effective training without requiring massive generic datasets. Experimental evaluation using the FLIP perceptual metric shows that our method achieves a mean error of 0.258 on 42 test triplets, outperforming state-of-the-art video interpolation RIFE (0.313, 17.5\% worse), traditional optical flow Lucas-Kanade (0.449, 42.6\% worse), and general frame synthesis CyclicGen (0.603, 57.2\% worse). This study shows that quality-over-quantity data curation and domain-specific architectural adaptations yield better interpolation quality than general-purpose methods trained on orders of magnitude more data, validating the data-centric AI paradigm for specialized visual domains. This is particularly important for small-to-medium-sized game development studios, where budget and time constraints are critical.
item.dc:creator: Kenneth Alonso, Gustavo Patow

item.title: HoOPOE: A Holography-Optimized Perceptual ObjectivE function
item.description: arXiv:2610.17474v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Holographic devices must reconstruct an entire light field given a finite number of spatial light modulator (SLM) pixels, and must do so using scalar-wave diffraction from coherent illumination alone. As a result, computer-generated holography (CGH) often has speckling artifacts. We propose HoOPOE (Holography-Optimized Perceptual ObjectivE function), a CGH-specific, perceptually-aware loss function that hides speckles from human vision. HoOPOE is effective for CGH optimizations because it accounts for the human visual system's sensitivity to spatio-temporal frequencies and color, and its parameters are tuned to maximize its performance as a loss function for CGH. We use HoOPOE to generate holograms for mesh-derived focal stacks. We then conduct a user study to benchmark HoOPOE-generated holograms against existing loss functions. HoOPOE yields the most visually pleasing results; users prefer HoOPOE 68% of the time over the next best objective function on average.
item.dc:creator: Ethan Chen, Xi Peng, Alexandre Chapiro, Dario Seyb, Michael Grundmann, Carl Marshall, Sushant Kondguli, Praneeth Chakravarthula, Yuhao Zhu

item.title: Integrating 3D Posture Neutralization with Statistical Shape Modeling for Head-Neck-Shoulder Ergonomic Design
item.description: arXiv:2610.17671v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The design of ergonomic products and workspaces requires a deep understanding of human anatomy and posture. In particular, the head-neck-shoulder region is critical for many applications such as cervical orthoses, helmets, and other head-worn or neck-worn devices. This paper presents a framework that integrates posture neutralization with statistical shape modeling (SSM) for the head-neck-shoulder (HNS) region. We acquire a single three-dimensional (3D) scan of the head-neck-shoulder region from each of 200 Chinese adults in a natural posture for each subject. Every scan is then posture-neutralized before SSM. We fit a parametric head-neck model to each scan to separate cervical pose from anatomy, and reset the cervical pose to a common neutral configuration, so that the resulting model captures anatomical shape variation rather than posture-induced deformation. The resulting shape space yields a standardized template and population-wide modes of variation, providing baselines for parametric ergonomic design. We further discuss how the model supports population coverage analysis and the design of products that accommodate anatomical diversity while maintaining neutral cervical posture.
item.dc:creator: Jinbo Luo, Hang Ren, Yadie Yang, Jie Zhang

item.title: TempFit: Panoptic Symbol Spotting via Template Fitting
item.description: arXiv:2610.17776v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce TempFit, a novel approach for the problem of Panoptic Symbol Spotting on CAD drawings. Existing methods treat symbol spotting as a per-primitive classification or mask-prediction task, with no explicit constraint enforcing that the primitives assigned to one instance form a spatially connected group. As a result, predictions may erroneously merge primitives from distant symbols into a single instance or fragment a coherent symbol across multiple predictions. Motivated by the professional "retrieve-and-transform" CAD design workflow, we reformulate this task as a Template Fitting problem, where each foreground instance is detected by retrieving and aligning a canonical template from a library, enforcing structural completeness by construction. Building on this formulation, we present an autoregressive transformer that unifies template retrieval and pose prediction within a single end-to-end pipeline. The framework treats the template library as an explicit geometric memory, parsing background regions in parallel via learnable background tokens and synthesizing foreground instances autoregressively while attending to template-specific geometry at each step. Experiments on FloorplanCAD and our newly collected IndustryCAD dataset, a more challenging benchmark with complex industrial symbols, heavy occlusion, and wide scale variation, demonstrate state-of-the-art performance with particularly large gains on IndustryCAD. Project page: https://tempfit-project.github.io/.
item.dc:creator: Honghao Xu, Hao Wang, Xiang Liu, Juzhan Xu, Manfred Lau, Kai Xu, Ruizhen Hu

item.title: Construction of Simple Quadrangulations of the Sphere at Skeletal Joints
item.description: arXiv:2610.17803v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a method for constructing a simple quadrangulation of the sphere from an unordered set of $n$ direction vectors, with application to parametric volumetric models of skeletal joints. We first select a quadrangulation encoding the joint topology by exhaustively enumerating candidate dual graphs, prioritizing convexity and regularity of the resulting quads. We then realize this topology on the sphere without crossings by solving a conflict-constrained assignment problem with lazy cyclic-order separation, and recover the corresponding primal graph. Experiments on direction sets from spherical Fibonacci sampling of size $3$ to $20$ show that the method robustly produces valid, high-quality quadrangulations across a range of input configurations. The resulting primal graph is directly converted into exact rational B\'ezier shell and column volumes, yielding a compact and precise volumetric representation of the joint. The approach extends naturally to multi-joint assemblies, enabling the construction of truss-based lattice structures within 3D domains.
item.dc:creator: Suil Hwang, Q Youn Hong

item.title: Content-Edited Layout Generation for Graphic Design
item.description: arXiv:2610.17905v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we formulate a novel form of conditional layout generation for graphic design, termed content-edited layout generation(CELG). CELG extends conventional content-aware layout generation (CLG), which generates a foreground layout for a fixed background image. The key distinction is that CELG treats the input image as an editable visual asset and, conditioned on a textual design intention and a foreground requirement that may be empty, produces an adapted background together with its layout. To study this task, we introduce Search-Compare-Edit(SCE), a data construction framework that supplies the paired supervision missing from existing design datasets. Starting from professional design canvases and their layouts, SCE synthesizes plausible pre-edit source images and corresponding editing instructions, yielding InstructEdit, a dataset of aligned source images, target canvases, instructions, and layouts. Based on the generated data, we train a two-flow multimodal flow matching model that couples a pretrained image editor with a layout flow transformer, enabling background editing and layout generation simultaneously within a unified framework that more closely reflects real-world design workflows. Our experiments systematically demonstrate the value of CELG as a distinct task and the performance advantages of the proposed model.
item.dc:creator: Shirong Yang, Zheyi Pan, Ying Cao

item.title: From Prototype to Massing: Learning Graph Correspondence for Scalable Facade Modeling
item.description: arXiv:2610.14098v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Facade articulation at building scale is usually resolved manually or through parametric systems that encode design intent as explicit rules. This paper investigates a complementary workflow in which a designer-authored prototype supplies transferable articulation logic. Prototype and target massing are represented as heterogeneous attributed graphs, and a Siamese graph attention network with instance-local triplet supervision embeds their segments in a shared metric space. Many-to-one nearest-neighbor retrieval then routes prototype Patterns to the larger target. On the original 85/15 within-corpus holdout, prototype-to-massing top-1 accuracy reached 96.5%, compared with a reported 76.5% raw-feature baseline. A Rhino demonstrator converts predicted correspondence into reusable facade Patterns, and qualitative applications on four built projects show the workflow across distinct massing organizations. The contribution is not automated facade generation, but an authoring model in which resolved geometry serves as a computational specification for project-scale propagation.
item.dc:creator: Yiliang Shao

item.title: SliderEdit++: Improved Slider Trajectories in Instruction-Based Image Editing
item.description: arXiv:2610.14253v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Slider-based control aims to give users continuous, fine-grained control over the intensity of individual edits in instruction-based image editing. However, existing approaches fail to deliver reliable continuous controllability: traversing a slider can produce abrupt visual jumps and non-monotonic changes, while jointly controlled sliders can interfere with one another. To systematically study these limitations, we introduce SlideBench, a comprehensive benchmark for continuous image editing spanning diverse editing categories and equipped with a unified suite of metrics quantifying monotonic progression, perceptual continuity, and inter-slider disentanglement. Building on these observations, we propose SliderEdit++, which explicitly regularizes the intermediate editing trajectory rather than supervising only its endpoints. Our method combines velocity- and semantic-space trajectory regularization with spectral control to encourage smooth, predictable slider traversal, together with a disentanglement objective that reduces interference between independently controlled edits. On SlideBench, SliderEdit++ achieves state-of-the-art performance, improving the overall score by 18.5% relative to the strongest baseline. At the same time, using a few-step editing backbone makes our method approximately 3x to 20x faster than existing slider-based approaches, enabling substantially more responsive interactive editing.
item.dc:creator: Arman Zarei, Sayan Nag, Bryan Wang, Franck Dernoncourt, Varun Manjunatha, Nedim Lipka, Soheil Feizi, Samyadeep Basu

item.title: Reels-RSI: Program-Level Self-Improvement for Code-Rendered Explainer Videos
item.description: arXiv:2610.14495v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Explainer videos -- a worked geometry problem, why the sky is blue, how a dynasty fell -- are usually one more target for pixel video generation. We argue they are a different kind of artifact: a program (script, storyboard and per-frame animation code) that a deterministic renderer turns into frames. A program can be read, diffed, tested and audited; pixels can only be watched. Reels-RSI is an open-source reel director for any agent harness; its self-improvement happens at the program level rather than in weights or prompts. Every revision pass is logged with a code snapshot; a retrospective pairs each check finding with the diff that fixed it and proposes lessons; a lesson that a static check can catch is compiled into a rule with a must-fail and a must-pass example, so the memory is unit-tested; and a rule learned today runs over everything made before it. A bounded, benchmark-gated step lets an agent rewrite the director's playbook, kept only when blind pairwise judgments on held-out topics prefer it; nothing enters memory without a human decision. Across 111 reels -- a field study, two playbook evolutions, a 2x2 memory ablation, a weaker director, a 48-reel learning curve and a judge-reliability study -- we find that the rule learned in the field caught four latent defects in frames authored before it existed and none after; that rules are an audit for a strong director (eight unguarded reels, no violation) and a guard for a weaker one (thirty violations unguarded versus five); that lessons shorten revision loops but do not compound or move the judge; and that the first rewrite's 11--1 verdict was a position bias in our vote design (judges pick the second-shown reel 62--81% of the time), masking scripts that traded thirteen facts for craft. We document four failure modes of the preference signal, which check caught each, and the fixes. Code, rules, lessons and data are public.
item.dc:creator: Wei Lin

item.title: Automatic assembly modeling through attention-based assembly feature mate prediction and assembly feature pattern recognition
item.description: arXiv:2610.14633v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Assembly modeling plays an important role in constructing product models, yet it is still mainly performed via interactive operations that are experience-dependent and labor-intensive. Data-driven strategies hold promise for automating this process; however, existing approaches either predict poses that cannot directly generate editable B-Rep assembly constraints or require prescribed part pairs or predefined assembly faces. To reduce the large candidate space of constraint prediction without predefined assembly faces, we propose a data-driven framework based on assembly feature mate prediction. The framework performs automatic assembly modeling from unassembled B-Rep parts, using assembly features to group the geometric entities of local mating interfaces and restrict candidate formation. Given the lack of suitable assembly feature annotations in existing datasets, we construct a large-scale dataset through an automatic annotation pipeline. Using the annotated dataset, we train an attention-based network to predict assembly feature mates, with Engineering Compatibility Fusion (ECF) incorporating explicit engineering compatibility into learned matching scores. To improve the accuracy of automatic assembly modeling, we use assembly feature patterns (AFPs) to guide the matching process. Finally, a post-processing search selects assembly feature mate and AFP mate candidates, whose associated constraints are generated and solved to complete assembly modeling. Experimental results show that the framework achieves assembly constraint accuracies of 74.79% on the six-assembly comparison set and 64.09% on the extended test set of 16 assemblies, which includes the comparison set. With ground-truth face labels supplied as additional input, the corresponding accuracies increase to 81.78% and 80.93%, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Ziheng Dai, Wanbin Pan, Zhihong Tang, Shuming Gao

item.title: Learning Dynamic Grasping
item.description: arXiv:2610.14848v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Synthesizing believable 4D hand-object grasping sequences is important for character animation, extended reality, and embodied agents. Grasping requires a hand to approach, contact, and lift or manipulate an object coherently. Existing synthesis methods often model only the final static grasp or rely on additional conditions, such as language, target grasps, or object trajectories, to specify the interaction. We instead study the underconstrained problem of generating a complete grasping motion from a single initial hand-object state. Our framework decouples hand-motion generation from object-motion recovery. Given an object point cloud in the initial wrist frame and the initial parameterized hand configuration, conditional flow matching predicts a sequence-level contact map and a hand pose at each normalized sequence time. This time-indexed formulation avoids the error accumulation of autoregressive rollout while representing the complete motion. We then infer an attachment frame and recover rigid-object motion through training-free, contact-guided weighted registration. We evaluate on held-out DexYCB objects and unseen object geometries reconstructed from in-the-wild videos by Open-CHOIR. Compared with LatentHOI, our method produces smoother hand and object motion in every setting, matches or improves on its contact and penetration metrics in the wild under a shared initialization, and is about 30x faster per generated frame. In a 15-participant study, our motions were preferred in roughly two thirds of (forced-choice pairwise) comparisons. Precise contact closure on novel geometry, however, remains a key open challenge.
item.dc:creator: Nga Kiu Kelly Ho, Yilin Liu, Hao Xu, Niloy J. Mitra

item.title: Gen Through the Lens: Camera-Controllable Video Generation via Cross-Coordinate Conditioning Fusion
item.description: arXiv:2610.15900v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present Gen Through the Lens, a camera-controllable image-to-video generation framework that synthesizes videos from a given reference image while enabling realistic and physically consistent camera operations. Unlike previous models that treat camera motion as abstract conditioning or rely on a single coordinate system, our approach explicitly decomposes and fuses control signals across three coordinate spaces: the camera coordinate (modeled by intrinsic parameters), the world coordinate (represented by spatial geometry hints), and the object coordinate (described by 3D bounding boxes of target subjects). Through cross-coordinate conditioning fusion, these heterogeneous cues are unified to guide the generative process, enabling precise control of camera motion, focus, and framing while preserving temporal and spatial coherence. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method produces controllable and visually consistent results across diverse camera operations, outperforming existing approaches in both realism and editability.
item.dc:creator: Shuai Li, Jinxu Xiang, Xinyuan Li, Hanlei Guo, Xiyang Tan, Alan Zhao, Xiaotong Zhao, Ran Zhang

item.title: AgentCue: Statistical Summaries for Guiding Decentralized Multi-Agent Self-Organization
item.description: arXiv:2610.16621v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-agent systems (MAS) combine multiple agents to solve complex tasks, and recent MAS scale to more than a thousand agents. At this scale, decentralized MAS remove the central orchestrator that assigns sub-tasks, and the agents, which we call workers, self-organize through their own choices of sub-tasks and collaborators on a shared board. As workers keep adding participation and collaboration records, however, the information explodes: workers spend more and more effort on reading the records of other workers, and self-organization loses efficiency. In the statistical view, we represent the execution history of an MAS by two continually updated networks, a collaboration network among workers and a participation network between workers and task types. We then propose AgentCue, a method built on a new latent space model that places workers and task types in a shared latent space. Each time the networks are updated, the estimated parameters of the latent space model form a compact and interpretable statistical summary, and workers use the statistical summary to choose sub-tasks and collaborators without repeated searches of the shared board. We establish the identifiability of the latent space model and non-asymptotic error bounds for the estimates under network increments, and we show that a fixed number of gradient updates after each network update suffices for the same error rate. Experiments on LongBench v2 Multi-Doc QA show that AgentCue achieves competitive effectiveness, efficiency, and interpretability.
item.dc:creator: Guojun Zhu, Xinyou Chen, Kejian Zhang, Sanguo Zhang, Doudou Zhou

item.title: Texture Interpolation as Texton Matching
item.description: arXiv:2610.18655v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Texture interpolation asks what should lie between two textures. Standard methods typically blend pixels or features at corresponding spatial locations, implicitly assuming that co-located elements should be mixed. For unrelated textures, however, this correspondence is arbitrary: a crack at one location has no particular relationship to a fiber at the same location in another image. We study whether this hidden pairing choice is itself a major determinant of interpolation quality. We represent textures as collections of local appearance vectors, or textons, and replace positional pairing with appearance-aware matching while keeping the encoder, representation, and decoder fixed. This isolates the effect of correspondence from changes in model capacity or training. Across texture pairs, appearance-aware matching consistently improves the distributional quality of interpolated midpoints over positional feature blending. Soft matching produces the strongest midpoint statistics, whereas one-to-one assignments yield more balanced transitions and closer agreement with the target endpoint. The same intervention also improves a second pretrained texture interpolator without retraining. These results identify correspondence as a first-class design choice in texture interpolation: meaningful transitions depend not only on how strongly two textures are mixed, but also on which local appearances are mixed with one another.
item.dc:creator: Ido Madar, Gal Oren, Shai Avidan

item.title: RoboSimStudio: An Interactive Toolkit for Rapid Real2Sim of Robot Manipulation Tasks
item.description: arXiv:2610.18835v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: It is difficult to accurately model the physics of the interaction between a robot and the objects it manipulates, including contact mechanics, coupled contact dynamics, deformations, stiffness and friction. We present RoboSimStudio (RSS), an interactive toolkit that makes choices of solver, contact model, and physical parameters explicit and editable, allowing both humans and coding agents to iteratively refine simulations based on observed physical behavior. We implement RSS with the open Newton physics simulation system and describe experiments with human-guided real2sim using (1) visual evaluation, (2) force-feedback and (3) agentic Real2Sim2Real. Code, video and additional information can be found on the project website.
item.dc:creator: Kaiyuan Chen, Shuangyu Xie, Uksang Yoo, Xinyue Zhu, Cael Magner, Alvin Zhu, Daehwa Kim, Eric Heiden, Erwin Coumans, Miles Macklin, Spencer Huang, Ken Goldberg

item.title: Cepheid: Decoupling Scale from Structure for Cross-Family Motion Completion
item.description: arXiv:2610.18871v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Sparse-to-dense motion completion recovers dense mesh motion from sparse vertex displacements. Residual priors trained on one geometry family frequently fail to beat parameter-free harmonic extension off-family. Moreover, cross-family training meets a scaling barrier: residual amplitude varies by more than an order of magnitude across geometry families and collapses as observations become denser. Since this scale depends on unknown target motion, it cannot be measured directly at test time. We decouple residual structure from physical scale by learning a dimensionless prior, estimating amplitude from observables and a lightweight correction fitted only on training sources. Our unified model surpasses harmonic extension across all evaluated families, including unseen cloth and legged bodies, without skeletons, registration, or cross-mesh correspondence. The same prior applies without retraining to point-tracked animal video and a robot grasping a soft body. Project page: https://su-terry.github.io/cepheid-website/
item.dc:creator: Chih-Hai Su, Tsung-Wei Ke, Yu-Lun Liu

item.title: SplatBus: A Gaussian Splatting Viewer Framework via GPU Interprocess Communication
item.description: arXiv:2601.15431v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Radiance field-based rendering methods have attracted significant interest from the computer vision and computer graphics communities. They enable high-fidelity reconstruction with complex real-world lighting effects, but at the cost of high rendering time. 3D Gaussian Splatting solves this issue with a rasterization-based approach for real-time rendering, enabling applications such as autonomous driving, robotics, virtual reality, and extended reality. However, due to the lack of format and rendering standardization, the ecosystem is fragmented into specific viewers. This makes it difficult to integrate these methods into traditional mesh-based rendering pipelines, which is a common use case for interactive applications. To address this limitation, we propose a framework that uses Nvidia's interprocess communication (IPC) APIs to provide an implementation-agnostic rendering server, enabling the results to be viewed in external clients such as Unity, Blender, and OpenGL viewers. The code is available at https://github.com/RockyXu66/splatbus.
item.dc:creator: Yinghan Xu, Th\'eo Morales, John Dingliana

item.title: IMAGAgent: Orchestrating Multi-Turn Image Editing via Constraint-Aware Planning and Reflection
item.description: arXiv:2603.29602v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Existing multi-turn image editing paradigms are often confined to isolated single-step execution. Due to a lack of context-awareness and closed-loop feedback mechanisms, they are prone to error accumulation and semantic drift during multi-turn interactions, ultimately resulting in severe structural distortion of the generated images. To address this, we propose IMAGAgent, a multi-turn image editing agent framework based on a ``plan--execute--reflect'' closed-loop mechanism that achieves deep synergy among instruction parsing, tool scheduling, and adaptive correction within a unified pipeline. Specifically, we first present a constraint-aware planning module that leverages a vision-language model (VLM) to precisely decompose complex natural language instructions into a series of executable sub-tasks, governed by target singularity, semantic atomicity, and visual perceptibility. Then, the tool-chain orchestration module dynamically constructs execution paths based on the current image, the current sub-task, and the historical context, enabling adaptive scheduling and collaborative operation among heterogeneous operation models covering image retrieval, segmentation, detection, and editing. Finally, we devise a multi-expert collaborative reflection mechanism in which a central large language model (LLM) synthesizes evaluations from multiple vision-language models into holistic feedback, triggering fine-grained self-correction and recording feedback outcomes to optimize future decisions. Extensive experiments on our constructed MTEditBench and the MagicBrush dataset demonstrate that IMAGAgent achieves performance significantly superior to existing methods in terms of instruction consistency, editing precision, and overall quality. The code is available at https://github.com/hackermmzz/IMAGAgent.
item.dc:creator: Fei Shen, Chengyu Xie, Lihong Wang, Zhanyi Zhang, Xin Jiang, Xiaoyu Du, Jinhui Tang, Tat-Seng Chua

item.title: GReFEM: Multimodal LLMs as Zero-Shot Semantic Assistants for Physics-Guided 3D Mesh Refinement
item.description: arXiv:2607.08798v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Adaptive volumetric finite element meshing traditionally requires iterative PDE solvers or heavily supervised, data-driven surrogates trained on large-scale simulation data. This work explores a significant question: can the high-level semantic understanding of off-the-shelf MLLMs serve as a viable, zero-shot geometric proxy for finite element mesh refinement? We introduce $\textbf{GReFEM}$ (Geometric Reasoning Enhanced Multimodal LLMs for Finite Element Meshing), a framework that utilizes MLLMs to visually localize stress-critical regions based on physics-guided textual prompts. To bridge the gap between 2D MLLM pre-training and 3D geometries, we introduce $\textit{orthoViews}$, a trained view-selection module that assists these MLLMs by maximizing the observability of key geometric features. We evaluate $\textbf{GReFEM}$ by computing finite-element error at stress concentrations, on diverse CAD mesh geometries under multiple loading cases, with MLLMs and prompt variants, against blind and load-informed geometric heuristics, solver-informed Zienkiewicz--Zhu (ZZ) refinement, and a retrained learned adaptive-meshing baseline, all at a matched element budget. Without any FEM solve or simulation training data, $\textbf{GReFEM}$ lowers the critical-region peak von Mises stress error relative to a blind geometric heuristic and to refinement driven by a coarse FEM solve, closing $58\%$ of the gap between the unrefined mesh and a reference-solve oracle, while a hand-derived analytical load-informed heuristic remains stronger and the learned baseline performs slightly better overall. With this we investigate their performance as semantic assistants in automated simulation workflows. Code is available at https://github.com/kbali1297/GReFEM
item.dc:creator: Kartik Bali, Mahish K. Guru, Christian J Cyron, Roland Aydin

item.title: Split Radiance Cascades: Real-Time Global Illumination via Sparse Radiance Probes
item.description: arXiv:2607.20384v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Radiance probe methods are a popular and well-tested approach for approximating diffuse global illumination for real-time graphics, but they commonly suffer from a lack of detail due to the large spacing between probes. Radiance Cascade (RC) fixes this by increasing spatial resolution and reducing angular resolution for light and occlusion from closer objects, which allows it to provide details at all scales without noise or aliasing. However, leading implementations of RC either run in 2D or screenspace, due to the prohibitive costs of storing high-detail volumetric radiance information. In this work, we adapt Radiance Cascades for accurate real-time 3D diffuse global illumination using a sparse hashmap to store world-space probes. We introduce ray splitting, a method for calculating radiance intervals used in RC by tracing rays from visible surfaces and calculating their contribution to cascades based on their hit distance. We evaluate our algorithm, Split Radiance Cascades, on a variety of scenes, and demonstrate that it can provide high-quality indirect illumination in both single-frame and temporally accumulated contexts.
item.dc:creator: Rouli Freeman, Alexander Sannikov, Joe Pitt-Francis

item.title: Sivia: Learning to Draw, Learning to Learn
item.description: arXiv:2609.33386v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A paper's overview figure is often the first thing readers see: it must explain the method correctly and look polished. We present Sivia, an overview-figure system that reads the paper, plans its relations, adapts visual organization from recent top-conference papers, and composes a design for image generation. Sivia improves with use through human-guided recursive self-improvement (RSI) at two levels: learning to draw revises its drawing skill from feedback on accuracy and presentation, and learning to learn revises the updater that proposes those revisions. A personal profile adapts presentation to its user's aesthetic preferences while the scientific content stays fixed. A diagnostic study of 1,964 overviews for 445 papers (17,973 relation judgments) shows that most errors are omissions and that source-derived relation plans raise required-relation accuracy (RRA) by up to 19.85 points. On 48 test papers, learning both levels reaches 93.54\% RRA, 15.31, 9.38, and 8.33 points above the initial skill, the Fixed-updater, and the GEPA baselines, while readability and visual quality rise from 3.95 and 4.00 to 4.70 and 4.78 on five-point scales. Learned presentation profiles raise liking from 4.02 to 4.73 and adoption from 34 to 45 of 48 tasks. Code and released artifacts are available at https://github.com/exsinger-hub/Sivia
item.dc:creator: Feng Yuan, Xinyi Gao, Zijun Sun, Haoyue Li, Menglei Hua, Xiao Li, Yifan Gao

item.title: Compositional Machine Design as Program Synthesis with LLMs
item.description: arXiv:2510.14980v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong abilities in writing and revising programs, yet many program-synthesis benchmarks still evaluate programs in symbolic or digital environments. We introduce compositional machine design, a physically grounded form of program synthesis where machines are written as programs that compose standardized parts, and success is determined by simulated physical behavior. To study this problem, we present BesiegeField, a testbed built on the machine-building game Besiege. In BesiegeField, LLM agents generate machine programs from textual functional demands, execute the resulting machines in simulation, and receive rewards and state feedback. We benchmark LLM agents across representative machine-design tasks under single-agent generation, iterative editing, and hierarchical workflows. Strong models recover task-relevant structures and sometimes achieve nontrivial physical performance, but often struggle with spatially precise assembly, mechanism-level planning, and translating feedback into useful structural edits. We further finetune Qwen2.5-14B, an open-source LLM, with reinforcement learning from simulation-derived rewards. We find that, under a fixed generation budget, RL improves the best machine discovered. We additionally evaluate human performance to provide a reference point for task difficulty. These results establish compositional machine design as a testbed for studying LLM agents that synthesize executable machine programs and improve them through physical feedback.
item.dc:creator: Wenqian Zhang, Yangyi Huang, Weiyang Liu, Zhen Liu

item.title: TopoPilot: Reliable Conversational Workflow Automation for Topological Data Analysis and Visualization
item.description: arXiv:2603.25063v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recent agentic systems demonstrate that large language models can generate complex codebases from natural language prompts. Despite this progress, they present reliability concerns for scientific visualization due to invalid operations, subtle errors, and failure to resolve underspecified inputs. These challenges are compounded in real-world workflows that exceed the complexity of standard benchmarks. In this work, we introduce TopoPilot, a reliable and extensible agentic framework for automating complex scientific visualization workflows. We focus on topological data analysis and visualization as a primary use case, while designing the framework to generalize to broader visualization domains. TopoPilot employs a two-agent architecture: an orchestrator translates user prompts into workflows composed of atomic backend actions, while a verifier evaluates workflows prior to execution. Its modular design isolates components and supports new topological descriptors and domain-specific workflows without modifying the core system. It also employs numerous deterministic guardrails to ensure semantic consistency and accurate execution. To systematically improve reliability, we develop a taxonomy of failure modes and employ targeted safeguards for each class of error. Across 1,000 simulated multi-turn conversations spanning 100 prompts, including adversarial and infeasible requests, TopoPilot achieves a success rate exceeding 95%, compared with under 50% for a baseline without comprehensive guardrails and verification. We also show that TopoPilot outperforms Claude Code and Codex on similar prompts in terms of accuracy, completion time, and token usage.
item.dc:creator: Nathaniel Gorski, Shusen Liu, Bei Wang

item.title: Feed-Forward 3D Scene Modeling: A Problem-Driven Perspective
item.description: arXiv:2604.14025v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Reconstructing 3D representations from 2D inputs is a fundamental task in computer vision and graphics, serving as a cornerstone for understanding and interacting with the physical world. While traditional methods achieve high fidelity, they are limited by slow per-scene optimization or category-specific training, which hinders their practical deployment and scalability. Hence, generalizable feed-forward 3D reconstruction has witnessed rapid development in recent years. By learning a model that maps images directly to 3D representations in a single forward pass, these methods enable efficient reconstruction and robust cross-scene generalization. Our survey is motivated by a critical observation: despite the diverse geometric output representations, ranging from implicit fields to explicit primitives, existing feed-forward approaches share similar high-level architectural patterns, such as image feature extraction backbones, multi-view information fusion mechanisms, and geometry-aware design principles. Consequently, we abstract away from these representation differences and instead focus on model design, proposing a novel taxonomy centered on model design strategies that are agnostic to the output format. Our proposed taxonomy organizes the research directions into five key problems that drive recent research development: feature enhancement, geometry awareness, model efficiency, augmentation strategies and temporal-aware models. To support this taxonomy with empirical grounding and standardized evaluation, we further comprehensively review related benchmarks and datasets, and extensively discuss and categorize real-world applications based on feed-forward 3D models. Finally, we outline future directions to address open challenges such as scalability, evaluation standards, and world modeling.
item.dc:creator: Weijie Wang, Qihang Cao, Sensen Gao, Donny Y. Chen, Haofei Xu, Wenjing Bian, Songyou Peng, Tat-Jen Cham, Chuanxia Zheng, Andreas Geiger, Jianfei Cai, Jia-Wang Bian, Bohan Zhuang

item.title: Lambda-Hold Control: Human-Like Movement Emerges from a Minimal Task Reward in Predictive Musculoskeletal Simulation
item.description: arXiv:2608.17030v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The massive overactuation in the human musculoskeletal system makes it challenging to train musculoskeletal models to generate human-like motion via reinforcement learning, primarily because exploration in the resulting high-dimensional and redundant action space is extremely inefficient. To address this problem, we propose the $\lambda$-hold controller, inspired by the equilibrium-point (EP) hypothesis, which has been widely supported by extensive evidence from human motor control studies. The policy's control variable is the per-muscle EP threshold length $\lambda$, from which a stretch-reflex recruitment law computes the muscle excitations automatically. Holding each $\lambda$ over an interval of the gait phase also sharply reduces the frequency at which the policy must be queried. Consequently, the controller, to our knowledge for the first time, enables a muscle-actuated skeletal model to learn human-like sprinting using only a minimal reward within an hour of training. The efficient exploration through the proposed $\lambda$-hold controller is not merely an engineering trick but an approach grounded in physiology, bringing together the EP hypothesis, intermittent control, and optimal feedback control. Beyond encapsulating human-like behavior in predictive simulation, this achievement contributes to developing a learnable model of the human motor controller.
item.dc:creator: Jun Hyuk Lee, Chihyeong Lee, Jooeun Ahn

item.title: A Benchmark for Spatially Grounded Gesture Generation
item.description: arXiv:2610.03105v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Communication in shared space interweaves verbal and non-verbal signals, and pointing gestures anchor language to the environment: "put the cup on that one" is uninterpretable without the gesture that fixes the referent. Yet no common framework exists for evaluating whether generated gestures indicate their intended referent; distributional metrics reward a gesture aimed at the wrong object as long as it looks natural. We introduce a benchmark for spatially grounded gesture generation, comprising ~2K pointing-annotated clips from naturalistic VR dialogue with ground-truth 3D referents, a task in which systems must decide when, how and where to point within conversational speech, and a protocol that separates temporal alignment, spatial grounding and perceived naturalness. We also provide a flow-matching baseline, MM-Conv-Flow. Evaluating it alongside an independent retrieval-based system and captured human motion, we find that geometric grounding can exceed that of human pointing without any gain in perceived naturalness, showing that referential gesture quality must be measured along separate dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Anna Deichler, Rishabh Dabral, Fethiye Irmak Dogan, Anindita Ghosh, Jonas Beskow
